finding: Description work id hashes the caller's spelling of the file name, so a re-run of the same file through a differently-cased path files a duplicate ticket
why: The folder half comes from `source.resolve()` (on-disk case) but the hashed file name is the unresolved `source.name`; on a case-insensitive filesystem (Windows, default macOS) the same file gets a new digest, the marker search misses, and a second ticket is created; the D-31 slug form lower-cased both halves so this is a regression, and it contradicts D-33 'A re-run of the same file gets the same id'.
fix: Resolve once (`resolved = source.resolve()`) and hash `f"{resolved.parent.name}/{resolved.name}"` (slug `resolved.stem`), plus a test that re-runs the file via a differently-cased path.
evidence: Code: `folder = source.resolve().parent.name` / `digest = hashlib.sha1(f"{folder}/{source.name}"...`. Probe (Windows, StubGitHub, run() helper): file created at docs/Export/DESCRIPTION.md -> ticket 1; re-run with path docs/export/description.md (resolve() -> ...\docs\Export\DESCRIPTION.md, .name -> 'description.md') prints 'PLAN: work id export_description-dd31686b; ticket to be created', 'STEP: ticket — 2 created'; stub.issues == ['1', '2'].

finding: The new 'names no ticket' refusal skips an empty `--key`, which still silently creates a new ticket
why: `if key and not given` treats `key=""` as no key at all, so `--key "$KEY"` with an empty variable creates (and moves the spec folder for) a fresh ticket instead of refusing, while `--key " "` and `--key #` are refused — the fix covers one sibling input and not the other.
fix: Test `key is not None` (`if key is not None and not given: raise Refused(...)`) and add `""` to the parametrized refusal test.
evidence: Probe via the test module's run(): key="" on StubGitHub -> code 0, 'STEP: ticket — 1 created', writes ['tracker_create', 'tracker_comment']; key="" on StubJira -> code 0, 'STEP: ticket — PROJ-1 created'; key="  " on StubJira -> code 1, 'REFUSED: `--key   ` names no ticket; nothing was written'.

finding: StubGitHub rewrites `ticket_key` before the shared stub records the call, so `stub.calls` no longer shows the key the code sent. Its copy of the adapter's `_number` is hand-written
why: A test reading `stub.calls` cannot tell whether the code sent `#5` or `5`. The hand copy can drift from `adapters/tracker/github-issues/api.py:_number`, which also strips leading `#`.
fix: Record the raw payload and normalize only for the stub's own lookup, or import the adapter's `_number` for the normalization.
evidence: `payload = dict(payload, ticket_key=str(payload["ticket_key"]).rsplit("#", 1)[-1])` then `return super().call(operation, payload)`; Stub.call: `self.calls.append((operation, json.loads(json.dumps(payload))))`
